        The Minnesota Vikings are adding to their receiving corps ahead of Monday night's matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Minnesota is signing former Pro Bowl receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to the 53-man roster, according to The Ringer. Minnesota signed Beckham to its practice squad on Oct. 7, roughly a week after he was released by the New York Giants. Beckham was targeted just once in three games with the Giants prior to his release. Beckham, who turned 34 on Nov. 5, made the Giants' initial 53-man roster after he missed the entire 2025 season. He played in nine games for the Dolphins in 2024 before being released in mid-December. 

                                    
                    Odell Beckham Jr.

Beckham had plenty of early success in the NFL with the Giants. He was named to the Pro Bowl during each of his first three seasons. Beckham later had a 1,000-yard season with the Browns (in 2019) and helped the Rams win the Super Bowl at the end of the 2021 season. During the Rams' Super Bowl win over the Bengals, Beckham had an early touchdown before he sustained an injury that sidelined him for the entire 2022 season. Beckham hasn't been the same player since that injury. 
Beckham will now look to help improve a Vikings offense that is just 27th in the NFL in scoring and 31st in passing. On Monday night, Minnesota will face a Bills defense that is 30th in the NFL in passing yards allowed and 27th in touchdown passes permitted.

title: SEC completes historic 'circle of chaos' as parity (and cannibalism?) define first-ever 9-game league slate - CBS Sports
description: A complete circle of chaos and widespread cannibalism won't keep the conference from strong College Football Play
body:
A complete circle of chaos and widespread cannibalism won't keep the conference from strong College Football Playoff representation
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:58 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        KNOXVILLE, Tenn. -- Kentucky coach Will Stein hasn't been in the SEC long, but he's already learned the company line."It's the closest thing to the NFL," he said Saturday night after his Wildcats took a 34-6 loss at Tennessee. "I've said that a million times. Everybody's good, everybody's got good players and good schemes."And now, everybody except Georgia also has at least two league losses. No. 6 Kentucky's 28-point defeat before a hostile "dark mode" crowd of 101,915 at Neyland Stadium dropped it to 7-2 (5-2 SEC). It also ensured that the two teams who eventually meet in the SEC Championship Game in Atlanta on Dec. 5 will have at least three combined league losses for only the second time since 2010.So robust is the SEC's parity that Saturday marked the completion of an SEC "circle of chaos." For just the third time since 1933 and for the first time in 20 years, everyone in the conference has a transitive victory over everyone else in the conference, per Gator Analytics.
This comes with three weeks of league play still ahead.It took Vanderbilt picking up its first conference win over a hobbled Mississippi State team to complete the circle. Since the 'Dores are finally on the board, it marks just the second time in a 10-season span that no SEC team is going to finish winless in league play.More SEC carnage aheadThe question now is how many will finish with 3-plus league losses during the SEC's first season with a 9-game conference schedule. All but five are already there.As teams head into a November stretch that often used to include a "buy" game against a Group of Six or FCS opponent, there are few reprieves ahead. 
Kentucky, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee comprise the SEC's contingent of two-loss teams coming out of Week 10. Of the four, three still play at least one opponent that is .500 or better in the conference.Of course, even playing a team with a sub .500 mark in conference action brings no guarantees.
As the SEC has often reminded us this year, its bottom half is dangerous. Florida (5-4, 3-4 SEC) and Auburn (5-4, 3-4) are fighting for bowl eligibility under first-year coaches, but they have combined for three wins over teams ranked inside the top 10 of the initial CFP Rankings.
If not for the conference's 10-2 mark against other Power Four leagues this season, this SEC cannibalism might raise questions over whether anyone in the league its truly good. But the conference destroyed its nonconference opposition, which has given it license to destroy itself without doing irreparable harm.Because of the SEC's schedule strength, even teams with early November records that would have relegated them to non-contender status in the past are very much alive for both the College Football Playoff and SEC Championship Game.It's like during the 2024-25 college basketball season, when the SEC posted a 59-19 record against other power conference teams during non-league play. If other leagues had a problem with the SEC earning a record 14 NCAA Tournament bids that season, they should have done something about it on the court in November and December.
If other leagues have a problem with the SEC potentially getting at least one 9-3 team in the 12-team CFP field, they should have done something about it in September.Life inside the circle is brutalAs Stein settled behind a makeshift media dais deep inside the bowels of Neyland Stadium, he was noticeably subdued. But even after his UK team was outscored 21-0 in the fourth quarter of his first SEC road loss as a head coach, the often fiery 37-year-old was not dejected. "I told the guys, we're 7-2 and 5-2 in the league," Stein said, relaying the postgame message he offered to his team. "Everything that we want is still right in front of us. We have a really tough test at home next week against Florida. We've got to reset our focus. It's a really tough league."
Kentucky arrived in Knoxville with the league's longest winning streak at six games and with aspirations of staying on pace with Georgia in the conference standings.It stayed within striking distance until a rare bout with turnovers eventually took its toll. As Rocky Top echoed through an emptying Neyland Stadium for the final time and Kentucky's players finished their retreat to the visiting locker room, the conference's other marquee matchup of the evening was still ongoing.Across the state of Tennessee and slightly to the south in Oxford, Mississippi, No. 2 Georgia's 42-7 beatdown of Ole Miss challenged the idea that no truly great teams exist in the SEC. The Bulldogs woke up Sunday as clear national title favorites (+240).
Yes, that's the same Georgia team that lost at home to Auburn just three weeks earlier. Such is life in the SEC circle of chaos.

        Penny Hardaway has made it clear in his time as coach at Memphis that he wants to schedule in a way that gives his program a chance to annually build an at-large resume for the NCAA Tournament despite playing in a conference that currently ranks ninth nationally, according to KenPom.com.The approach hasn't always gone well.Last season, for instance, it went horribly wrong as his Tigers lost seven of their first 11 non-league games en route to what ended up being the program's worst season in 56 years. Things got so bad Hardaway became the face of the hot seat list heading into his ninth year at his alma mater, and yet he still once again assembled a non-league schedule so tough that, this time last week, KenPom was projecting the Tigers as underdogs in each of their first four games.
        
            
                Rare opening-week title game rematch doubles as a familiar warning: UConn is yet again a national title threat
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
But Memphis is 2-0.Somehow, someway, Memphis is 2-0.We are now seven full days into the 2026-27 season, and you can reasonably argue nobody had a better first week than Hardaway's Tigers. They opened Monday with an 80-76 neutral-court win over No. 18 Iowa State, then backed that upset Saturday with an 89-88 victory at FedExForum over a VCU team that's picked to win the Atlantic 10 and ranked 57th at KenPom.It's still early, sure. And everybody schedules with different motivations, obviously. That acknowledged, what you're about to read is true: in this moment, Memphis is the only team in Division I men's basketball with A) a victory over an opponent ranked in the AP poll, and B) another victory over another opponent ranked in the top 60 at KenPom.
"I'm just so thankful," said an emotional Jayden Reid, the transfer from Northwestern who scored 32 points against VCU, buried the game-winning free throws in the final seconds, and is now averaging 29.0 points, 4.0 assists and 2.5 steals for the undefeated Tigers. "I'm just thankful, man. ... I'm just thankful for God. He put me in a great position, coming to Memphis out the portal. I'm so thankful for my coaches, my teammates. It's a big-time win at home."To understand how big this start is for Hardaway, you have to understand how rough things have gotten for him. He's the program's greatest alum, everybody's favorite Memphis graduate and someone who would've been a Naismith Memorial Hall of Fame player if injuries had not robbed him of his abilities too early. Before the city had the Grizzlies as an NBA franchise, Penny was the city's NBA franchise.He matters that much to his hometown.So, yeah, it's been a tough go over the past eight years that have featured just one conference championship to go with four fifth-place-or-lower finishes in the American. The Tigers have only made three NCAA Tournament appearances under Hardaway and won just one game in that postseason event. There have been more top-ranked recruiting classes than wins in the bracket. There have been more NCAA investigations than wins in the bracket.
Every bit of this is depressing to type -- first and foremost as a Memphis alum, but also as a columnist/analyst who very publicly suggested Hardaway should be the person to replace Tubby Smith back in 2018. Things have not gone smoothly -- or the way I hoped they'd go, or the way I anticipated them going. Put DraftKings on it, and, if we're being honest, Hardaway would've been considered an underdog, just a week ago, to still be the Memphis coach on April 1, 2027.This is a make-or-break year, undeniably.And who knows where it's headed, still? Long way to go and all that. But, one week in, you can make the case, all things considered, that no team in the country is off to a better start than Memphis, which is No. 26 in Sunday morning's updated CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings.Up next for the Tigers is another big test -- more specifically, their biggest test of the season to date. Memphis will play Vanderbilt inside Memorial Gym on Tuesday. The Commodores are 2-0 and ranked 24th in the Top 25 And 1.
Is a 3-0 start on tap for Memphis?According to the computers, no. But, don't forget, just a week ago, the computers had Memphis starting 0-4. Now Memphis is 2-0. So it's possible the computers just don't have a great grasp for these Tigers quite yet, which is both understandable and also the thing that could reconnect the city to the coach and program that once had its heart. title: NC State finalizing deal to hire Philip Rivers as next coach - CBS Sports
description: Rivers, who starred in the NFL and for four years as NC State's quarterback, is expected to return to his alma ma
body:
Rivers, who starred in the NFL and for four years as NC State's quarterback, is expected to return to his alma mater
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Philip Rivers is finalizing a deal to return to Raleigh as NC State's next coach, returning to the school where he became a star in college to try to revive the Wolfpack in the ACC, 247Sports reports.Rivers would take over for Dave Doeren, who was fired following a Week 8 loss to Stanford that brought his career record in Raleigh to 98-73, and he will be tasked with getting the Wolfpack to the next level as an ACC contender. The NC State job will be Rivers' first college coaching position, but he's coached high school football at St. Michael Catholic in Fairhope, Alabama, since 2021. A gamble on star powerRather than take a swing on a rising star coordinator or try to bring in an established head coach, NC State is opting to go a third route with a Wolfpack legend to try and get more investment into the program. What Rivers lacks in experience, NC State hopes he can make up for with enthusiasm and by getting the Wolfpack's top boosters to open their wallets a bit more to build a roster that can compete in the ACC. Rivers was a four-year starter at NC State from 2000 to 2003, completing 63.6% of his passes for 13,484 yards, 95 touchdowns and 34 interceptions in his time playing for the late Chuck Amato. The 2002 season remains the high point of NC State's history as a program, going 11-3 with a Gator Bowl win. That season stands as the only time the Wolfpack have won 10 games in a campaign. Under Doeren, NC State won nine games five times but could never break through that 10-win barrier. Doeren unquestionably raised the floor at NC State, making the Wolfpack a consistent bowl team and a perennial top-25 team for much of his tenure. Over the past three seasons, that standard had slipped, and there was a sense of apathy around the program, with fans resigned to their fate as members of the ACC's middle class. 
In the NIL era, apathy from the fan base isn't something a program can afford, and Rivers' first job will be to rally the donor base and secure a cash influx to quickly upgrade the roster. Unlike a new coach coming in from another program, Rivers won't be able to bring a roster with him in the portal that knows his system, which means if NC State is going to hit the ground running in his first season, they're going to need investment to bring in upgrades from the portal. While Rivers is a bit of a mystery in terms of scheme, he'll have a familiar face joining him in Raleigh. His son, four-star quarterback Gunner Rivers, remains committed to the Wolfpack and will be quite familiar with his father's offense after four years of running it at the high school level. Can Rivers spark a new era?If nothing else, the Rivers experiment will be fascinating to watch. Will he be a Deion Sanders type? A coach who can inject immediate life into a program (with the help of a highly touted quarterback for a son) but may struggle to sustain that, especially once his son moves on. Will he be a Trent Dilfer? A former NFL quarterback turned high school coach who ends up in over his head in terms of running a college program. 
Or perhaps he can eclipse both of them and become an NC State legend a second time by leading the Wolfpack to a new level of success in the 24-team College Football Playoff era. Time will tell, but there will be no shortage of eyeballs on what Rivers does in Raleigh, more than 20 years after he starred for them.

description: It pays to be rich.Big NIL spenders typically land the best transfer and recruiting classes. That talent typically leads to more wins, r
body:
It pays to be rich.Big NIL spenders typically land the best transfer and recruiting classes. That talent typically leads to more wins, right? Yup. Turns out, most programs that spent a lot of money this fall haven't necessarily wasted their cash.Twelve teams spent about $40 million on players this season, according to CBS Sports' reporting in the preseason. That's a nice number to start with in this 12-team playoff era, and unsurprisingly those rich programs are (mostly) winning more games. Only two of those 12 teams enter Week 11 outside CFP contention: Michigan (5-4) and Texas A&M (4-5). (More on their stumbles later) Four others have three losses, and we suspect at least one of them will become the first three-loss team in the CFP: LSU, Ohio State, Oregon and Ole Miss.
The two remaining undefeated teams (Utah and UCLA) are not in the grouping, of course. And among the seven programs that spent $40 million or more, only two have one loss: Miami and Notre Dame, which met Saturday.Georgia is just below the $40 million line and also has one loss, and will likely have the No. 1 ranking later today.Combined, the 12 teams have won 72.2% of their games.Investing heavily in the roster yields more wins. Imagine that: a straightforward, albeit challenging, path to success for struggling programs. Some can charge the gated communities, but those teams – Wake Forest, Kentucky, Utah – are rare outliers.
CFB's 12 most expensive rosters (ranked by record)TeamRecordGeorgia8-1Miami8-1Notre Dame8-1Texas7-2Tennessee7-2USC7-2LSU6-3Ohio State6-3Oregon6-3Ole Miss6-3Michigan5-4Texas A&M4-5The undefeated teams don't deserve the No. 1 spotWhile two teams in the West remain unbeaten, a separate juggernaut is tearing through the nation's best conference and dominating the final month of the regular season.No. 2 Georgia demolished No. 10 Ole Miss 42-7 in Oxford on Saturday. No matter how wild 2026 has been across the sport, Georgia's October home loss to Auburn is this season's greatest mystery. That loss feels distant after these past two weeks."I feel like we could have put up 60," Georgia defensive back KJ Bolden said Saturday. "We got a little relaxed. We could have pitched a shutout. I don't have regular standards like everybody else. Our standards are pretty high here."Utah and UCLA deserve flowers, but the eyes don't lie when you look at Georgia. The Bulldogs have returned to smothering opponents and stealing souls. Four of Gunner Stockton's nine pass completions went to Talyn Taylor for 140 yards and three touchdowns. Efficient. Deadly.Georgia has won seven of its last eight against AP-ranked teams. The leash holding the Bulldogs back in the pantheon is their recent CFP performances, including the season-ender against Ole Miss in last season's quarterfinals. But there was progress, and something tells us they'll take another step this year with a deeper postseason run.Another frustrating end for MizzouMissouri set itself up to enter the CFP discussion in the final month of the regular season, but choked again at home while lifting Texas back into contender status.Both programs entered with two losses and followed their scripts to perfection Saturday: the Longhorns won their sixth straight game against an AP-ranked team and the Tigers fell to 1-11 in their last 12 against ranked opponents. The Tigers had opportunities, of course, and squandered them. Austin Simmons was picked off in a comeback attempt, leading to a short touchdown run that helped Texas escape with a 34-20 win.Mizzou received huge news on the eve of the showdown when quarterback Austin Simmons decided to return for the 2027 season. But will that lead to wins against ranked teams? The Paper Tigers need something to get them over the hump. Maybe another year with Simmons will get them there, but not this season. The Tigers travel to No. 2 Georgia and host top-10 Kentucky over the next two weeks. They could sneak into the field, but nothing shows us they're capable. Mizzou's CFP chances jump from 1.8% to 9.4% with a win next week between the hedges, according to CBS Sports' Forecasting and Projections. That's not happening.Mizzou fans must be banging their heads against the wall.UCLA is not 2025 Indiana, but …The Bruins (9-0, 6-0 Big Ten) are still undefeated, folks. They pulled off another impressive road win, pulling away for a 34-20 victory at Minnesota, to start 9-0 for the first time since 1998.UCLA handed Minnesota, which knocked off Michigan and Iowa earlier this season, its first home conference loss in two years.Bob Chesney is only the second coach in FBS history to start 9-0 after taking over a program that lost nine games the year prior. That other coach is Curt Cignetti, of course.This Bruins team is not loaded at receiver, and especially at quarterback, like last season's national champion Hoosiers, but it does look like an amalgamation of Indiana 2026 and the 2024 Hoosiers. That's a good thing, of course, but it might not lead to a Big Ten title.It's remarkable how UCLA keeps winning with defense, a solid running attack and an inconsistent quarterback capable of hitting explosive plays at any moment. Backup Ty Dieffenbach's misfires and passer rating will never wow you, but he's been clutch in place of injured starter Nico Iamaleava. He threw back-to-back 75-yard touchdown passes to Aidan Mizell to break the tie in the fourth quarter. With 303 passing yards on just 8 of 16 attempts, his performance proved historic, marking the lowest completion total by any FBS player to reach 300 passing yards in a game since 2000.Chesney has to be the leader for national coach of the year.Don't sleep on SMU's ACC, playoff chancesMany wrote off SMU as a playoff contender eight days ago, but the Mustangs are alive again after blowing out Virginia Tech.SMU's playoff chances jumped to 8.8% with the 51-28 win, and they could skyrocket to 20.4% if they knock off Wake Forest next Saturday in Dallas. A win would put SMU in a tie for second place in the ACC and would set up a tiebreaker advantage against the Demon Deacons.Remember, the Mustangs also have a trip to Notre Dame on the schedule Nov. 21. A win in South Bend would change everything. That's if the defense can step up and QB Kevin Jennings remains consistent. He's thrown 13 touchdowns against only one interception over the last five games. The defense ranks 54th in scoring.'Stangs ain't done runnin' in the CFP or ACC races.Lane Train is off the tracks againLane Kiffin is the third-highest-paid coach in the sport and the only one in the top five without a major conference title or playoff win.That trend will likely continue following a third loss, a 31-13 embarrassment at home against Alabama. LSU entered Saturday a 5.5-point favorite, but couldn't do anything offensively --  Kiffin's bread and butter -- and the LSU faithful poured out of Tiger Stadium in the fourth quarter.Kiffin fell to 0-6 against the Tide as a head coach. Four of those losses have been by double digits. The closest he came to defeating the Tide was in 2009, his first try, in a 12-10 loss as Tennessee's head coach.USC's Lincoln Riley is the sole coach whose underwhelming results match Kiffin's massive salary. Despite making $11.5 million as the sixth-highest-paid coach in college football, Riley remains stuck on the playoff bubble. And how in the world is Kiffin convincing Hollywood elite like Kevin Costner to usher him into the stadium when Riley is posted up in LA? Maybe The Postman mistakenly thought the "LA" abbreviation referred to Kiffin's old Los Angeles address.Texas A&M's Mike Elko is not far behind at $10.8 million, ranking ninth. His Aggies have five losses, big production costs and terrible box office returns. Kiffin's entire career has been all flash. At some point, being handed the nation's most talented roster will result in a postseason run for Kiffin, but the slow burn to that marker -- and his defection from Ole Miss and previous late-season meltdowns -- continue to be a troubling trend for the Bayou Barker.One-and-done(s)?Some results are so nonsensical, you wonder if it really happened. We got two this week.Tulsa 60, Tulane 10. Michigan State 15, Michigan 6.What did both games have in common? The losers were led by first-year coaches. Both deserve a hard look.
Kyle Whittingham was supposed to provide a soft transition after the tragedy that was Sherrone Moore's era, and he's done that off the field, but he has somehow made the on-field product worse. The Wolverines' offense is so abysmal, it's breaking records set before World War II. Michigan has now failed to score seven points in back-to-back home games for the first time since 1936. Pairing that mess with the benching of a high-priced quarterback makes it clear that the financial investment hasn't offset the administrative headaches, nor has bringing in a coach who was heading toward retirement in Utah.The reality is Michigan should be 4-5 with a loss to Western Michigan, but Big Ten officials saved the Wolverines from that embarrassment with their clock snafu. Not many of us saw this coming in Ann Arbor, but most did predict failure in New Orleans. 
First-year Tulane coach Will Hall failed as head coach at Southern Miss, going 18-35 with one winning season. Now, he has taken one of the premier, best-funded programs in the Group of Six and run it straight into the dirt. Just one year after making the playoff, Tulane finds itself sitting at a disappointing 4-5.Saturday's result was so bad that Tulane athletic director David Harris released a statement. It was mostly platitudes about hard work and expecting better, but at least he said he was "embarrassed by what transpired on the field." He still couldn't muster the strength to say the score, only referencing that the result was "alarming given the point differential."

title: Notre Dame 'A' gets mark, Ohio State 'F' on Week 10 report card - CBS Sports
description: A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 10 action
body:
A look at how national championship contenders fared in Week 10 action
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:26 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With No. 11 Notre Dame's season potentially hanging in the balance Saturday night, the Fighting Irish could ill-afford to squander the only remaining opportunity on their schedule to secure a marquee win. It was a simple pass/fail assignment. Though it got uncomfortable in the fourth quarter, Marcus Freeman's club passed the test.Typically, 'A' grades are reserved for teams that thoroughly dominate their opponents in most key statistical categories. Notre Dame didn't quite do that against Miami, but it won the game. This showdown was never going to be about style points. It was about doing what it takes to arrive at Selection Sunday with a marquee victory.To be fair, Notre Dame did lead 24-3 at one point against the nation's No. 1 ranked team, showing glimpses of total domination. Eventually, Miami got back into the game, requiring the Fighting Irish to make a couple of late stops. It wasn't perfect. But when you consider the stakes and caliber of opponent, it was 'A' worthy showing.We are handing out grades evaluating every team that started or ended the day with national championship odds of +3000 or better. No. 4 Indiana (+850) had a bye
2026 national championship odds listed below courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Teams listed in order of their AP Top 25 ranking.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 MiamiGrade: C  Result: 31-24 loss at Notre Dame  Title odds: +800Predictably, Miami's offense started out looking like mess without star receiver Malachi Toney. The Hurricanes sputtered and stammered for the entire first half and fell behind 24-3 before getting back into the game. But the hole was simply too big. Defensively, the Hurricanes' shortcomings in the secondary were exposed by Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr, who surpassed 300 yards passing for the first time this season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 GeorgiaGrade: A+  Result: 42-7 win at Ole Miss  Title odds: +240Georgia piled up 221 yards in the first quarter alone and opened up a 21-0 lead one minute into the second quarter. Unlike Texas, which let the Rebels rally a couple of weeks ago, the Bulldogs never let up. UGA's No. 2 spot in the initial CFP Rankings felt a little premature, given the lack of depth to Georgia's accomplishments beyond its Alabama win. But this showing proved the predictive metrics right. When Georgia shows up -- like it showed up in a hostile environment against a good Ole Miss team -- it is the best team in college football. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 UtahGrade: B+  Result: 28-20 win vs. BYU  Title odds: +2200BYU reeled off 20 straight points to close the first half -- rallying from an early 14-0 deficit -- before Utah's defense turned ruthless and bought the offense time to recover from a prolonged lull. 
The Utes picked off BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier three times in the second half alone. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier survived a shaky stretch and got loose with his legs at the end of the third quarter to help Utah retake the lead for good. It wasn't always pretty, but both units produced some bright moments. That's what they call complementary football.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 AlabamaGrade: A  Result: 31-13 win at LSU  Title odds: +650Alabama's defense mastered the art of bending without breaking while limiting LSU to one touchdown on four red-zone trips. The Crimson Tide defense also flexed in key downs, holding the Tigers to 5 of 19 on third- and fourth-down plays. Offensively, the Crimson Tide ran just 53 plays, but Keelon Russell delivered three touchdown passes. In his first game back from injury, star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams also made an impact with a rushing touchdown and a huge punt return in the fourth quarter. The run game wasn't great. But within the context of Alabama being an underdog and coming away with an 18-point road win over LSU, that's not a grade killer.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 TexasGrade: A-  Result: 34-20 win at Missouri  Title odds: +1100Arch Manning played a turnover-free game while throwing for 297 yards and three touchdowns as he guided the Longhorns back from a 20-13 deficit. He was sacked three times amid some indecision and continued struggles from the Longhorns' offensive line. But considering that Cam Coleman, his most-talented receiver, was out due to injury, this was a good day for him. The Texas defense didn't necessarily wreak havoc, but its only sack of the day was a huge one in the fourth quarter that helped flip the field, leading to a go-ahead Texas touchdown.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 Ole MissGrade: F  Result: 42-7 loss vs. Georgia  Title odds: +2700Not even the great Trinidad Chambliss could dig Ole Miss out of this hole. Georgia outclassed the Rebels on their home field in every facet of the game, dealing first-year Ole Miss coach Pete Golding a humbling dose of revenge. When the Rebels beat Georgia in last year's CFP quarterfinals, they had a more disruptive defense and a more dynamic offense. This time around, the Bulldogs exposed deficiencies on both sides of the ball. Ole Miss gave up way too many explosive plays and had no answers in one of the most stunningly lopsided outcomes of the year.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 Notre DameGrade: A  Result: 31-24 win vs. Miami  Title odds: +380Notre Dame's defense made sure nothing came easy for Miami's vaunted offense in the first half. The showing was highlighted by a goal-line stand in the second quarter as the Irish turned a first-and-goal from the 1-yard line for the 'Canes into a chip-shot field goal. 
Offensively, quarterback CJ Carr played arguably his best game of the season while shaking off a couple of recent inefficient performances. In a borderline must-win game, the Fighting Irish came through. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Ohio StateGrade: FResult: 41-28 loss vs. OregonTitle odds: +xThe absence of starting quarterback Julian Sayin remains an obvious hindrance for Ohio State, but that's to be expected. The vulnerability of the Buckeyes' defense is the more stunning revelation. The nation's preseason No. 1 team has allowed 30-plus points in back-to-back regular season losses for the first time since 1990. Oregon reeled off three straight long touchdown drives over the second and third quarters to extinguish any hope for a team playing with a freshman quarterback. Two late Ohio State scores made this look more respectable than it was.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 14 LSUGrade: C-Result: 31-13 loss vs. AlabamaTitle odds: +1800All the good vibes LSU amassed during convincing wins over Mississippi State and Auburn dissipated in a sea of missed opportunities during a loss that left the Tigers' CFP hopes all but extinguished. LSU ventured into Alabama territory eight times and reached the red zone four times. It came away with just 13 points while stumbling to a 0 for 4 mark on fourth-down plays. LSU's run defense was solid, but it gave up too many explosive passing plays while suffering a rare loss as a home favorite.

title: Tom Fornelli's CFP Vibe Check: Dawgs barking in Georgia, Oregon returns from dead - CBS Sports
description: Plus, which teams belong in Alabama's College Football Playoff 'Tide pod' and why BYU's hopes are now on the rope
body:
Plus, which teams belong in Alabama's College Football Playoff 'Tide pod' and why BYU's hopes are now on the ropes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 8, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:08 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Every week the CFP Vibe Check tries to put its finger on where things stand in the College Football Playoff race without overreacting to what it just saw, but also probably overreacting to everything it just saw. There will be a new No. 1 this week, both in the polls that do not matter in determining the national champion and in the one that does. There will be debate over whether it should be No. 2 Georgia or No. 3 Utah moving up, both of which won Saturday against top-10 teams. Someone will probably argue on No. 8 UCLA's behalf, though they'll largely be ignored.Regardless of who deserves it most, or who winds up getting it, I know which team I'm the most confident in right now: the Georgia Bulldogs.As I watched Georgia decimate Ole Miss 42-7 in Oxford (OK, so I only watched the first half), a thought occurred to me. Is it not possible that we all spent so much time talking amongst each other about how there are no elite teams this year that we collectively ignored the one right in front of us?
Were we so blinded by the disappointments of many preseason contenders that we ignored the fact that one team was chugging right along the whole time, looking pretty damned dominant?
Again, Georgia didn't just beat Ole Miss on Saturday. It went into Ole Miss' house and beat the living snot out of the Rebels. After forcing an Ole Miss three-and-out on the opening possession of the game, Georgia scored a touchdown on each of its first three possessions. It was 21-0 in the blink of an eye. Nate Frazier and the Dawgs' rushing attack did anything they damn well pleased. Gunner Stockton only threw the ball 15 times, but finished with 186 yards and 4 touchdowns. You don't have to throw a lot when you average 12.4 yards per attempt and throw a touchdown on 26.7% of your attempts.Defensively, things didn't get much better for Ole Miss after the opening three-and-out. They were held to 252 yards. They couldn't run the ball, nor could they throw it effectively. This was not a repeat of the two incredible shootouts we saw last year. This was one team letting another know that it was much better, and that all your foolish hopes and dreams were just that: foolish.
I can see why we may have ignored Georgia's dominance earlier in the season. It's hard to get overly excited when the wins are coming against Western Kentucky, Arkansas, Oklahoma and Vanderbilt. But since that soft start, the Dawgs have taken down Alabama in Tuscaloosa and Ole Miss in Oxford. They spanked Florida in Atlanta. And while there was the loss against Auburn, did you watch the game? No offense to Auburn, as we never ask anybody to apologize for winning, but that game had a lot more to do with Georgia giving it away than Auburn winning it.Georgia is basically one Gunner Stockton running into his teammate's backside and fumbling the ball away from being 9-0 right now. Even in their loss, they were the better team!Perhaps it's true that in this era of college football, we'll never see the truly dominant teams of the past again. But when I look at Georgia compared to everybody else, I see a team whose "worst" is far better than anybody else's.
In a season where it feels like you can't take anything for granted, Georgia strikes me as the most reliable team in the country.The Alabama Question
No team caught more flak in the first College Football Playoff Rankings than No. 5 Alabama. The Crimson Tide were No. 9 in the major opinion polls, but No. 5 in the CFP, a full eight spots above a Tennessee team that beat them by 16 points. It was the biggest surprise of the rankings, and when the hivemind is surprised, it usually responds with indignation.So what do we do with them now? Alabama went to Baton Rouge and did the thing it seemingly does every time it goes to Baton Rouge these days: it beat LSU 31-13. But it was an odd 31-13 win. If you look at the box score, you might be confused by what you see. LSU ran 81 plays to Alabama's 53. LSU outgained the Tide 457 yards to 285. 
The problem is LSU didn't score, and that's kind of important! Alabama reached the red zone three times and left with 21 points. LSU reached the red zone four times and left with 10. It turned the ball over on downs once and fumbled a second time. LSU was 0-for-4 overall on fourth downs. It moved the ball, but in crunch time, when it really needed it, it failed.So while Alabama didn't dominate the box score, it controlled the game and made the plays LSU didn't. But here's where things could get weird. There were seven teams between Alabama and Tennessee in last week's poll, and four of them (Kentucky, BYU, Ole Miss, and Ohio State) lost. Tennessee won. It beat Kentucky. That win gives Tennessee a "better" win than any Alabama has, plus the Vols have the head-to-head. So what if those four losses by other teams put Tennessee in the same pod as Alabama now? Remember, the committee said they didn't use the head-to-head result between them last week because they weren't in the same pod, but now they should be.
And Texas, which beat Tennessee, will be in that pod too. So how does this work if they're all in the same pod? Which head-to-head means more? And how do the resumes work?The point I'm trying to make, and one that shows you how comical this entire process truly is, is that Alabama went on the road and beat No. 14 LSU by 18 points and could very well drop in the rankings. Last week they were overrated, and now after their best win of the year, they may be underrated.What a system we created for ourselves.Oregon is back from the dead
Two weeks ago in this column, after an 11-point loss on the road to Illinois, I wrote about the death of No. 23 Oregon's hopes and dreams. That's a whoops on my part! The Ducks beat No. 12 Ohio State 41-28 on Saturday, and the game was not as close as the score suggests. Ohio State scored two touchdowns in garbage time to do a little damage control on their resume. Whether the committee will buy it or not remains to be seen.
As for the Ducks, plenty of eyebrows were raised when they appeared in last week's rankings. They were 5-3 with two losses to unranked teams in Illinois and Oklahoma State. They had fired their offensive coordinator. All hope seemed lost.Seemed is the important word, because after beating Ohio State to get to 6-3, the Ducks are still in the race. They can still get to Indianapolis and play for a Big Ten title as long as they win out and get help elsewhere. Their final three games of the season are against Michigan, Michigan State and Washington. Only the Michigan State game is on the road. The prospect of winning out isn't exactly a long shot. Reaching the Big Ten Championship might be, but even if they don't, it's not entirely out of the question that they could get an at-large at 9-3.By the time the season ends, those losses to Oklahoma State and Illinois could look a lot better. Oklahoma State is 6-3 and still alive in the Big 12 race. Illinois has won four straight to improve to 6-3. Both could be ranked on Tuesday night. If they are, and Oregon suddenly finds itself with three losses to ranked teams and with wins over Boise State, USC and Ohio State, they will climb toward at-large territory.
And if you don't want to take my word for it, check your local sportsbook. Heading into the weekend, Oregon's odds of making the field were +2000 (4.8%) at DraftKings. After beating Ohio State, they're now set at +280 (26.3%).BYU is on the ropes
Utah won The Holy War 28-20 in one of the most entertaining games of the day, and it might've crushed BYU's playoff hopes in the process. While BYU's win over Notre Dame looks even better after the Irish took down Miami in South Bend, I'm not optimistic the Cougars can get into the field without a lot of help elsewhere.The committee already had BYU at No. 9 with the Notre Dame win. That put them close to the bubble, and the Utah loss will likely take them out of the top 12 in this week's rankings. And when you look at BYU's remaining schedule, I don't know if there's anything on it that will help their cause.
It's hard to see the committee fawning over wins against Baylor, Cincinnati and Kansas.It doesn't help matters that so many teams are jumbled at the top of the Big 12 standings. BYU is one of five teams at 4-2 in conference play, and they're all behind 6-0 Utah and 5-1 Texas Tech, which survived a scare against West Virginia.Considering how Tech has played lately, it's not ludicrous to believe it will lose another game. Hell, it might lose on the road next week to Oklahoma State. I won't even pretend to know the tiebreakers for how the Big 12 will settle all these things if multiple teams are tied for second place, which seems somewhat likely at this point.
All I know is that if BYU doesn't win those tiebreakers and get a second crack at Utah in the Big 12 Championship, it will be very difficult to get back into the field.Rest in CFPeaceEach week for the rest of the season, we shall recognize the schools who saw their playoff hopes die over the weekendCincinnatiFloridaMichiganMinnesotaOregon StateUNLVVirginia TechWeek 11 Vibe ShiftersA look ahead to the five games on next week's slate most likely to impact the playoff raceTexas at LSUUtah at ArizonaUSC at IndianaTexas Tech at Oklahoma StateBaylor at BYUThis week's CFP ProjectionThis is a projection of what I expect the top 12 to be Tuesday nightGeorgiaUtahNotre DameMiamiIndianaAlabamaTexasUCLATennesseeKentuckyTexas TechWake ForestBoise State remains the highest-ranked G6 team and takes the final spot in the field.
